transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-09-22 17:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Lena Ortiz (Redwood AE), Marcus Lee (Redwood CSM), Aisha Rahman (Redwood SE), Tom Gardner (Equinox CTO), Priya Shah (Head of Data), Miguel Alvarez (DevOps), Sophie Chen (PM)

Summary (auto): Kickoff to align onboarding plan and pilot scope. Discussed SSO/SCIM, dedicated vs hosted, security controls, and pilot success metrics. Next steps: share docs, schedule deep dive, provide sample data and network diagram.

Transcript:
00:00 Lena Ortiz: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, this is Lena from Redwood, im the AE on the account, joining with Marcus and Aisha. how's everyone doing?
00:06 Tom Gardner: Good, thanks. appreciate you all. we had a quick prep with Sophie earlier, excited to get moving.
00:12 Marcus Lee: Cool, quick intros, and then we'll go into scope. I'm Marcus, customer success, i'll be your primary point for onboarding.
00:18 Aisha Rahman: Hi all, Aisha here, solutions eng, i'll be owning the tech hookups and the benchmark runs.
00:24 Sophie Chen: Sophie from product — we're focused on improving product search and site chat.
00:28 Priya Shah: Priya — head of data, i'll share data access details.
00:31 Miguel Alvarez: Miguel — ops, i'll be doing the network/VPC side.
00:35 Lena Ortiz: Great. Agenda — confirm pilot scope, auth and security (SSO/SCIM, KMS), infra options (hosted vs dedicated), timeline and success metrics, and action items. any additions?
00:44 Tom Gardner: No, that lines up.
00:46 Lena Ortiz: Cool. So to start, what's the primary success metric for the pilot? Sophie?
00:52 Sophie Chen: We're looking at a 20% improvement in search relevance (as judged by our internal relevance score) and reduce time to first meaningful result in the chat flow. also cost per 1k requests should be within reason — we have a rough budget.
01:05 Priya Shah: For metrics, we'll provide labeled relevance sets, and we expect the model responses to be PII-safe — so data handling is a concern.
01:12 Aisha Rahman: Got it. For that we typically recommend embeddings for search and a smaller context chat model, we can run both in the pilot. question on data residency — do you need in-region hosting?
01:23 Tom Gardner: Yes, EU residency for part of our traffic. most of our users are US/EU.
01:28 Marcus Lee: We can map routing by region — Redwood supports region-aware routing, and for enterprise we can do dedicated pools in region.
01:35 Miguel Alvarez: For network, we prefer VPC peering to keep traffic on our cloud VPC, is that an option?
01:40 Aisha Rahman: Yes, private deployment options exist — we have VPC peering for Dedicated, and a Private deployment option for on-prem later. For the initial pilot we usually do hosted to move fast, or dedicated if they need isolation.
01:52 Tom Gardner: Cost's a big factor — we have procurement constraints. What's the delta between hosted and dedicated?
01:59 Lena Ortiz: Hosted is usage-based, quickest to start. Dedicated is reserved capacity — higher minimums but predictable throughput and often better per-token economics for steady loads. we can share sample pricing.
02:12 Sophie Chen: Could we start hosted for a short evaluation and then move to dedicated if numbers look good?
02:17 Marcus Lee: That's a common path. For the pilot, we recommend a two-week hosted evaluation + a short benchmark run with your sample traffic, then we can size a Dedicated pool if you decide to commit.
02:29 Priya Shah: Security checklist — SOC 2, KMS, audit logs, and SAML SSO — those are high priorities for us.
02:36 Aisha Rahman: We're SOC 2 compliant, support customer-managed KMS, and provide detailed audit logs. SAML/SSO and SCIM for user provisioning are supported. we'll share our security pack and answers to your questionnaire.
02:48 Miguel Alvarez: On the VPC side, what's the setup latency look like for peering? we have change windows and firewall review.
02:55 Marcus Lee: Usually peering can be done in a few days once we have the network diagram and a contact for firewall rules.
03:02 Tom Gardner: We'll need that contact — Miguel will own the firewall rules.
03:06 Miguel Alvarez: okay i'll sync with you after the call.
03:09 Lena Ortiz: Great. Aisha — can you walk through the integration steps?
03:12 Aisha Rahman: Sure. Step one: we provide an SDK and quickstart repo, you can run a hosted key immediately. step two: ingest your sample dataset for embeddings; we recommend a batch run to generate embeddings. step three: set up the chat route and attach a model from our catalog. we'll instrument tracing to capture latency and token usage. for benchmarking we typically run synthetic traffic and replay a subset of your logs.
03:38 Sophie Chen: How accurate is the replay? we want representative latency numbers.
03:41 Aisha Rahman: We can match request distribution and sequence lengths; it won't be perfect but it's a good predictor. also we recommend enabling KV cache and prefix caching — that reduces per-token cost for repeated prompts.
03:54 Priya Shah: About KMS, do you have a bring-your-own-key flow?
03:57 Aisha Rahman: Yes, we have BYOK via customer KMS (AWS KMS/Azure Key Vault) for Dedicated and Private deployments. hosted supports server-side encryption and we can discuss BYOK for enterprise contracts.
04:10 Tom Gardner: Good. Any red flags on compliance for EU data?
04:14 Marcus Lee: We support regional hosting and audit logs; for strict residency we suggest Dedicated in the EU region or our Private option. we'll loop in security docs after the call.
04:24 Sophie Chen: For pilot scope, specifically we want embeddings for product search on the web catalog and chat for shopper assistance on the checkout flow. target is to process 10k embedding calls/day during the pilot and chat traffic of about 200 QPS peak for the test window.
04:40 Aisha Rahman: 200 QPS peak is doable; we'll size the benchmark to simulate that and advise on batching and concurrency settings.
04:48 Miguel Alvarez: For VPC peering we need IP ranges and FQDNs — we'll need those details.
04:52 Lena Ortiz: We'll provide a network checklist. I'll drop a link after the call.
04:56 Tom Gardner: On the timeline: procurement wants a 6-week window to get legal and finance approvals. can we align pilot start after that?
05:04 Marcus Lee: Totally. we can start initial hosted access before procurement finishes so your engineers can smoke-test. the full pilot benchmark can wait until agreements are signed.
05:14 Sophie Chen: Can we get a sample SOW or timeline?
05:17 Lena Ortiz: Yes, I'll send a proposed timeline and SOW template.
05:21 Priya Shah: Questions around PII — can the models be prevented from seeing certain fields? we have customer emails and order IDs in context sometimes.
05:29 Aisha Rahman: You can sanitize before sending, or use tokenization/redaction. For Dedicated/Private we can also restrict logging and set retention policies; audit logs will show who accessed what.
05:40 Tom Gardner: Great. any integration complexity with our existing infra? we use GCP mainly and have a GKE cluster for the app.
05:48 Aisha Rahman: We have SDKs for node/python and a REST API; for GCP you'll mostly call the hosted endpoints or route via VPC peering. We can provide a reference adapter if you want tight coupling with GKE.
05:58 Miguel Alvarez: Are there any requirements for egress IP ranges?
06:01 Marcus Lee: We'll provide the egress IPs for peering; you'll need to allow them in firewall rules.
06:05 Sophie Chen: Any notes on rate limits for the hosted trial?
06:09 Lena Ortiz: Trial keys start with a modest rate limit but we can bump it for pilot runs. if you go dedicated, we set the pool to handle your target QPS.
06:18 Tom Gardner: On pricing, can you send ballpark for 10k embeddings/day and 200 QPS chat?
06:23 Lena Ortiz: We'll run a rough estimate — Aisha will take sample sizes and run a cost projection. Marcus will include pricing tiers for hosted vs dedicated.
06:30 Aisha Rahman: Also will include optimization suggestions: quantization options for chat, batching for embeddings, and prefix caching for chat to cut costs.
06:39 Priya Shah: For security questionnaire, who's the contact?
06:41 Marcus Lee: I'll be primary, but our security lead is cc'd in the reply. we'll send the completed questionnaire within 48 hours.
06:48 Tom Gardner: Cool. Any blockers we see right now?
06:51 Sophie Chen: procurement timeline is the only blocker plus network firewall approvals.
06:55 Lena Ortiz: Ok, recap of next steps: Lena will share onboarding guide, SSO docs, SOW and network checklist; Marcus will send security questionnaire answers and pricing; Aisha will run latency/cost estimate once you share sample workload; Tom/Miguel will provide dataset and network diagram.
07:12 Miguel Alvarez: i'll get the network diagram to you by Friday.
07:15 Tom Gardner: i'll coordinate the dataset and give access to a sanitized sample.
07:19 Lena Ortiz: Perfect. we'll schedule the deep technical dive next week — Aisha, what's your availability?
07:24 Aisha Rahman: I'm free Tuesday/Wednesday mornings PST.
07:27 Sophie Chen: Tuesday morning works for us.
07:29 Lena Ortiz: Ok, we'll lock Tuesday 09:00 PST for the deep dive.
07:33 Marcus Lee: I'll send calendar invites and include the security pack link: drive.redwood.com/onboarding/equinox (note: placeholder).
07:40 Tom Gardner: Thanks everyone.
07:42 Lena Ortiz: Thanks all, talk soon.

Meeting End.
